s.t: Long ago, a troll made a mirror.
s.fr: Il y avait autrefois un troll qui fabriqua un miroir.

s.t: This troll loved to trick and laugh at people.
s.fr: Ce troll aimait tromper et se moquer des gens.

s.t: The mirror changed how things looked.
s.fr: Le miroir changeait l’apparence des choses.

s.t: Good things looked bad in the mirror.
s.fr: Les bonnes choses semblaient mauvaises dans le miroir.

s.t: A kind face looked cruel in the mirror.
s.fr: Un visage aimable semblait cruel dans le miroir.

s.t: The mirror made bad things look worse.
s.fr: Le miroir faisait paraître les mauvaises choses encore pires.

paras.summary: Long ago, a trickster troll made a magic mirror that turned good things bad, even a kind face cruel, and made bad things worse.

s.t: The troll carried the mirror from town to town.
s.fr: Le troll porta le miroir de ville en ville.

s.t: He looked at what the mirror showed and laughed.
s.fr: Il regardait ce que le miroir montrait et riait.

s.t: One day, the troll climbed a mountain with the mirror.
s.fr: Un jour, le troll gravit une montagne avec le miroir.

s.t: He held the mirror up to look at the whole world.
s.fr: Il leva le miroir pour regarder le monde entier.

paras.summary: The troll carries the mirror town to town, laughing at what it shows, until he climbs a mountain to view the whole world.

s.t: The mirror grew heavy in his hands.
s.fr: Le miroir devint lourd dans ses mains.

s.t: It slipped and fell.
s.fr: Il glissa et tomba.

s.t: The mirror broke into small splinters on the rocks.
s.fr: Le miroir se brisa en petits éclats sur les rochers.

s.t: A cold wind carried the splinters across the world.
s.fr: Un vent froid porta les éclats à travers le monde.

s.t: A splinter in the eye made everything look bad.
s.fr: Un éclat dans l’œil faisait tout paraître mauvais.

s.t: A splinter in the heart made it cold.
s.fr: Un éclat dans le cœur le rendait froid.

paras.summary: The mirror grows heavy, slips, and breaks into splinters; a cold wind scatters them, and a splinter in the eye or heart makes things bad and cold.

s.t: In a small town, Kai and Gerda lived in two houses, side by side.
s.fr: Dans une petite ville, Kai et Gerda vivaient dans deux maisons, côte à côte.

s.t: Each house had a box of roses by its window.
s.fr: Chaque maison avait une caisse de roses près de sa fenêtre.

s.t: The two boxes had a board between them.
s.fr: Les deux caisses avaient une planche entre elles.

s.t: Kai and Gerda climbed across the board each day.
s.fr: Kai et Gerda traversaient la planche chaque jour.

s.t: They loved each other like brother and sister.
s.fr: Ils s’aimaient comme frère et sœur.

paras.summary: In a small town, neighbors Kai and Gerda live side by side, each house with a rose box joined by a board they climb daily, loving each other like siblings.

s.t: In winter, Kai's grandmother told them of the Snow Queen by the fire.
s.fr: En hiver, la grand-mère de Kai leur parla de la Reine des Neiges près du feu.

s.t: The Snow Queen lived in the snow and cold.
s.fr: La Reine des Neiges vivait dans la neige et le froid.

s.t: "She looked in at windows and made them cold with frost," said grandmother.
s.fr: « Elle regardait par les fenêtres et les rendait froides avec le givre, » dit grand-mère.

s.t: "She had a palace of ice, up in the north," grandmother said.
s.fr: « Elle avait un palais de glace, là-haut dans le nord, » dit grand-mère.

paras.summary: In winter, grandmother tells them of the Snow Queen, who lives in the cold, frosts windows she looks in at, and has an ice palace far north.

s.t: Kai looked at the frost on his window.
s.fr: Kai regarda le givre sur sa fenêtre.

s.t: Kai said he would put the Snow Queen by the warm fire.
s.fr: Kai dit qu’il mettrait la Reine des Neiges près du feu chaud.

s.t: Gerda laughed at this.
s.fr: Gerda rit de cela.

s.t: Kai and Gerda looked at their roses each day.
s.fr: Kai et Gerda regardaient leurs roses chaque jour.

paras.summary: Kai jokes he would put the Snow Queen by the fire, making Gerda laugh, and they look at their roses.

s.t: One cold winter night, Kai sat by his small window.
s.fr: Un froid soir d’hiver, Kai était assis près de sa petite fenêtre.

s.t: A cold wind blew a small splinter into Kai's eye.
s.fr: Un vent froid souffla une petite éclat dans l’œil de Kai.

s.t: Kai rubbed his eye with his hand, but the splinter stayed.
s.fr: Kai se frotta l’œil avec sa main, mais l’éclat resta.

s.t: That night, another splinter went into Kai's heart, and it stayed.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, une autre éclat entra dans le cœur de Kai, et elle y resta.

paras.summary: One winter night, a cold wind blows a splinter into Kai's eye as he sits by his window, and another goes into his heart that night.

s.t: The splinter in his eye made Kai see only what was bad.
s.fr: L’éclat dans son œil fit Kai voir seulement ce qui était mauvais.

s.t: The splinter in his heart made it cold, like the wind and the snow.
s.fr: L’éclat dans son cœur le rendit froid, comme le vent et la neige.

s.t: Kai's heart was cold like the snow, so he no longer loved Gerda.
s.fr: Le cœur de Kai était froid comme la neige, alors il n’aimait plus Gerda.

paras.summary: The splinter in his eye makes Kai see only bad, and the one in his heart turns it cold, so he no longer loves Gerda.

s.t: That day, Kai looked at Gerda's roses and said they were bad.
s.fr: Ce jour-là, Kai regarda les roses de Gerda et dit qu’elles étaient mauvaises.

s.t: He pulled the roses from their box and threw them.
s.fr: Il arracha les roses de leur boîte et les jeta.

paras.summary: That day, Kai calls Gerda's roses bad and pulls them from their box.

s.t: "Stop!" Gerda said to Kai, but Kai only laughed.
s.fr: « Arrête ! » dit Gerda à Kai, mais Kai ne fit que rire.

s.t: Gerda did not want this bad change, but Kai would not stop.
s.fr: Gerda ne voulait pas ce mauvais changement, mais Kai ne voulait pas s’arrêter.

s.t: Kai no longer wanted to sit by the roses with Gerda.
s.fr: Kai ne voulait plus s’asseoir près des roses avec Gerda.

s.t: Gerda did not know why Kai had changed.
s.fr: Gerda ne savait pas pourquoi Kai avait changé.

paras.summary: Kai only laughs when Gerda tells him to stop, no longer wanting to sit by the roses with her, and she cannot see why he changed.

s.t: Winter came, and snow lay on the town.
s.fr: L’hiver arriva, et la neige recouvrit la ville.

s.t: Boys carried their sleds to the town square.
s.fr: Des garçons portèrent leurs luges à la place de la ville.

s.t: Kai went to the square with his sled.
s.fr: Kai alla à la place avec sa traîneau.

s.t: A white sledge came fast into the square.
s.fr: Un grand traîneau blanc entra rapidement dans la place.

s.t: A driver in white fur sat in the sledge.
s.fr: Un conducteur en fourrure blanche était assis dans le traîneau.

s.t: Kai tied his sled to the white sledge.
s.fr: Kai attacha sa traîneau au grand traîneau blanc.

s.t: The sledge flew out of the square and into the town.
s.fr: Le traîneau s’élança hors de la place et dans la ville.

paras.summary: Winter comes, and boys carry sleds to the town square; Kai goes too, and when a white sledge driven by a white-furred figure enters, he ties his sled to it, and it flies out of the square.

s.t: Kai wanted to go home, afraid of the fast ride.
s.fr: Kai voulait rentrer chez lui, effrayé par la course rapide.

s.t: He thought of his warm house and grandmother by the fire.
s.fr: Il pensa à sa maison chaude et à sa grand-mère près du feu.

s.t: The sledge went out of the town, into the snow.
s.fr: Le traîneau sortit de la ville, dans la neige.

paras.summary: Afraid, Kai wants to go home and thinks of his warm house and grandmother as the sledge leaves town.

s.t: Kai's hands were too cold to move, and the cold wind hurt his face.
s.fr: Les mains de Kai étaient trop froides pour bouger, et le vent froid blessa son visage.

s.t: Kai called out, afraid, but no one heard him.
s.fr: Kai cria, effrayé, mais personne ne l’entendit.

s.t: The sledge stopped, and the driver looked at Kai.
s.fr: Le traîneau s’arrêta, et le conducteur regarda Kai.

s.t: The driver was the Snow Queen, in white fur.
s.fr: Le conducteur était la Reine des Neiges, en fourrure blanche.

s.t: Her eyes were as cold as the snow and the wind.
s.fr: Ses yeux étaient aussi froids que la neige et le vent.

s.t: The Snow Queen put Kai into her sledge and wrapped him in fur.
s.fr: La Reine des Neiges mit Kai dans son traîneau et l’enveloppa dans de la fourrure.

paras.summary: Kai's hands are too cold to move, his face hurt by wind, so he calls out but no one hears; the sledge stops, its driver the Snow Queen, who puts Kai in and wraps him in fur.

s.t: In the cold night, the Snow Queen kissed Kai, and the cold left him.
s.fr: Dans la froide nuit, la Reine des Neiges embrassa Kai, et le froid le quitta.

s.t: The kiss made Kai forget Gerda, his grandmother, and his warm home.
s.fr: Le baiser fit oublier à Kai Gerda, sa grand-mère, et sa maison chaude.

s.t: The sledge flew north, and Kai was gone from the cold town.
s.fr: Le traîneau vola vers le nord, et Kai avait disparu de la froide ville.

s.t: Grandmother and Gerda stayed by day and by night, but Kai did not come home.
s.fr: Grand-mère et Gerda attendirent jour et nuit, mais Kai ne rentra pas.

s.t: People in the cold town said that Kai had fallen and was gone from home.
s.fr: Les gens de la froide ville dirent que Kai était tombé et avait disparu de chez lui.

s.t: Gerda did not believe this, for she had not seen it.
s.fr: Gerda ne crut pas cela, car elle ne l’avait pas vu.

paras.summary: In the cold night the Snow Queen kisses Kai, and the cold leaves him but the kiss makes him forget Gerda, his grandmother, and home, and the sledge flies north with him gone; though people say he fell and is lost, Gerda refuses to believe it, not having seen it herself.

s.t: Spring came, and the snow melted from the town and the small house.
s.fr: Le printemps arriva, et la neige fondit sur la ville et la petite maison.

s.t: Their roses bloomed in the window boxes that spring.
s.fr: Leurs roses fleurirent dans les jardinières de fenêtre ce printemps-là.

s.t: Gerda looked at the roses in the window and thought of Kai and of home.
s.fr: Gerda regarda les roses dans la fenêtre et pensa à Kai et à la maison.

paras.summary: Spring comes and the snow melts; the roses bloom again, and Gerda looks at them and thinks of Kai and home.

s.t: "I will go and find Kai now," Gerda said to grandmother by the fire.
s.fr: « Je vais aller trouver Kai maintenant, » dit Gerda à grand-mère près du feu.

s.t: Grandmother did not think Gerda would find Kai.
s.fr: Grand-mère ne pensait pas que Gerda trouverait Kai.

s.t: Gerda put on warm clothes and left the small house alone that cold day.
s.fr: Gerda mit des vêtements chauds et quitta la petite maison seule ce jour-là froid.

s.t: She went for days, north, into the cold snow, to look for Kai.
s.fr: Elle marcha pendant des jours, vers le nord, dans la neige froide, pour chercher Kai.

paras.summary: Gerda tells grandmother she will find Kai, and despite grandmother's doubt, she puts on warm clothes, leaves alone, and walks north for days into the cold to find him.

s.t: Gerda walked on and came to a great town with a palace.
s.fr: Gerda continua à marcher et arriva dans une grande ville avec un palais.

s.t: Gerda had walked for many days, and she was tired and cold.
s.fr: Gerda avait marché pendant de nombreux jours, et elle était fatiguée et froide.

s.t: That night, Gerda went into the palace to look for Kai.
s.fr: Ce soir-là, Gerda entra dans le palais pour chercher Kai.

s.t: She came to a room where a prince and princess were asleep.
s.fr: Elle arriva dans une pièce où un prince et une princesse dormaient.

s.t: Gerda called out for Kai, and the prince and princess woke.
s.fr: Gerda appela Kai, et le prince et la princesse se réveillèrent.

paras.summary: Gerda walks on, tired and cold, to a great town with a palace, where that night she looks for Kai and finds a sleeping prince and princess who wake when she calls his name.

s.t: But the prince was not Kai, only a boy that looked like him.
s.fr: Mais le prince n’était pas Kai, seulement un garçon qui lui ressemblait.

s.t: Gerda told the prince and princess about Kai and the Snow Queen.
s.fr: Gerda parla au prince et à la princesse de Kai et de la Reine des Neiges.

s.t: The prince and princess were kind, and they listened to her tale.
s.fr: Le prince et la princesse étaient aimables, et ils écoutèrent son récit.

s.t: They believed her tale of the cold Snow Queen.
s.fr: Ils crurent son récit de la froide Reine des Neiges.

paras.summary: Gerda tells the prince and princess about Kai and the Snow Queen, and they are kind, so they listen and believe her tale.

s.t: The next day, they gave Gerda warm clothes for her walk north.
s.fr: Le lendemain, ils donnèrent à Gerda des vêtements chauds pour sa marche vers le nord.

s.t: They gave her a golden coach to ride north, too.
s.fr: Ils lui donnèrent aussi un carrosse doré pour voyager vers le nord.

s.t: Gerda thanked the prince and princess and rode north in the coach.
s.fr: Gerda remercia le prince et la princesse et repartit vers le nord dans le carrosse.

s.t: The golden coach carried Gerda north, into the cold and snow.
s.fr: Le carrosse doré porta Gerda vers le nord, dans le froid et la neige.

paras.summary: The next day they give Gerda warm clothes and a golden coach for the road north, and she thanks them and rides into the cold and snow.

s.t: The golden coach went into a forest, and Gerda was cold and afraid.
s.fr: Le carrosse doré entra dans une forêt, et Gerda avait froid et peur.

s.t: Many robbers came out of the dark forest and stopped the coach.
s.fr: Beaucoup de brigands sortirent de la sombre forêt et arrêtèrent le carrosse.

s.t: An old robber woman looked into the coach at Gerda.
s.fr: Une vieille femme brigand regarda dans le carrosse vers Gerda.

s.t: She pulled out a long knife to hurt Gerda for the golden coach.
s.fr: Elle sortit un long couteau pour blesser Gerda à cause du carrosse doré.

s.t: But the old robber woman had a daughter.
s.fr: Mais la vieille femme brigand avait une fille.

paras.summary: The golden coach enters a forest, and Gerda is cold and afraid when many robbers stop it; an old robber woman looks in and pulls a knife to hurt her for the coach.

s.t: The daughter was a rough girl that carried a knife.
s.fr: La fille était une fille rude qui portait un couteau.

s.t: "Stop! I want her!" the daughter said to her mother.
s.fr: « Arrête ! Je la veux ! » dit-elle à sa mère.

s.t: The daughter stopped her mother's knife with her hand.
s.fr: La fille arrêta le couteau de sa mère avec sa main.

s.t: The robber girl was rough, but she smiled at Gerda.
s.fr: La fille brigand était rude, mais elle sourit à Gerda.

s.t: The robber girl had Gerda now, not her old mother.
s.fr: La fille brigand avait Gerda maintenant, pas sa vieille mère.

s.t: The old robber woman did not want this, but she let Gerda go.
s.fr: La vieille femme brigand ne voulait pas cela, mais elle laissa Gerda partir.

paras.summary: But the woman's rough daughter, who carries a knife, says she wants Gerda and stops her mother's knife with her hand; smiling despite her roughness, the girl now has Gerda instead of her unwilling mother, who lets her go.

s.t: The robber girl led Gerda to a castle in the forest.
s.fr: La fille du brigand conduisit Gerda à un château dans la forêt.

s.t: "You will live with me in this castle now," the robber girl said.
s.fr: « Tu vivras avec moi dans ce château maintenant, » dit la fille du brigand.

s.t: Night fell as they came to the castle, and Gerda stayed close to the girl.
s.fr: La nuit tomba quand ils arrivèrent au château, et Gerda resta près de la fille.

paras.summary: The rough girl leads Gerda to a forest castle, saying she will live there now, and as night falls Gerda stays close to her.

s.t: The robber girl's castle held many robbers.
s.fr: Le château de la fille du brigand abritait beaucoup de brigands.

s.t: The robber girl led Gerda to a corner of the castle.
s.fr: La fille du brigand conduisit Gerda dans un coin du château.

s.t: She kept many animals in this castle, from the forest.
s.fr: Elle gardait beaucoup d’animaux dans ce château, venus de la forêt.

s.t: Wood pigeons sat in a cage in the castle.
s.fr: Des pigeons ramiers étaient assis dans une cage dans le château.

s.t: A reindeer stood tied by a rope in the corner.
s.fr: Un renne se tenait attaché par une corde dans le coin.

paras.summary: Inside the noisy castle, the robber girl takes Gerda to a corner where she keeps forest animals, with wood pigeons in a cage and a reindeer tied by a rope.

s.t: "The reindeer came from the north," the robber girl said.
s.fr: « Le renne venait du nord, » dit la fille du brigand.

s.t: She held her knife near the reindeer, and it did not move.
s.fr: Elle tint son couteau près du renne, et il ne bougea pas.

s.t: That night, Gerda and the robber girl lay on a bed of straw.
s.fr: Cette nuit-là, Gerda et la fille du brigand s’allongèrent sur un lit de paille.

paras.summary: The reindeer came from the north, she says, kept still by her knife, and that night she and Gerda lie on straw.

s.t: The robber girl kept her knife in her hand, near Gerda, that night.
s.fr: La fille du brigand garda son couteau dans sa main, près de Gerda, cette nuit-là.

s.t: "If anyone comes near you, I will use this," she said to Gerda.
s.fr: « Si quelqu’un s’approche de toi, j’utiliserai ceci », dit-elle à Gerda.

s.t: Gerda was afraid to move in this castle, but not afraid of the robber girl.
s.fr: Gerda avait peur de bouger dans ce château, mais n’avait pas peur de la fille du brigand.

s.t: "Why do you want to find this boy?" the robber girl asked.
s.fr: « Pourquoi veux-tu trouver ce garçon ? » demanda la fille du brigand.

s.t: Gerda told her of Kai, the splinters, and the Snow Queen's sledge that night.
s.fr: Gerda lui parla de Kai, des éclats, et du traîneau de la Reine des Neiges cette nuit-là.

s.t: The robber girl listened and said nothing.
s.fr: La fille du brigand écouta et ne dit rien.

paras.summary: That night the girl keeps her knife near Gerda, warning she'll use it on anyone near, and though Gerda is afraid to move she isn't afraid of the girl, who asks why she seeks this boy, hears of Kai and the Snow Queen's sledge, and says nothing.

s.t: The next day, Gerda asked the wood pigeons if they had seen Kai.
s.fr: Le lendemain, Gerda demanda aux pigeons ramiers s’ils avaient vu Kai.

s.t: "We saw a sled tied to a white sledge," the pigeons said.
s.fr: « Nous avons vu un traîneau attaché à un grand traîneau blanc », dirent les pigeons.

s.t: "It flew over the forest and went north," they said.
s.fr: « Il vola au-dessus de la forêt et alla vers le nord », dirent-ils.

s.t: The reindeer said he knew the way to the north.
s.fr: Le renne dit qu’il connaissait le chemin vers le nord.

paras.summary: The pigeons tell Gerda they saw a sled tied to a white sledge fly north over the forest, and the reindeer says he knows the way.

s.t: "The robbers tied me in this castle," the reindeer said.
s.fr: « Les brigands m’ont attaché dans ce château », dit le renne.

s.t: "Go with the reindeer," the robber girl said.
s.fr: « Pars avec le renne, » dit la fille du brigand.

s.t: She cut the rope from the reindeer and helped him go.
s.fr: Elle coupa la corde du renne et l’aida à partir.

s.t: The robber girl gave Gerda warm mittens and warm clothes for the way.
s.fr: La fille du brigand donna à Gerda de chaudes moufles et de chauds vêtements pour le chemin.

paras.summary: The reindeer, tied here by the robbers, is freed by the girl, who cuts his rope and gives Gerda warm mittens and clothes for the way.

s.t: She helped Gerda climb onto the reindeer's warm back, with the mittens.
s.fr: Elle aida Gerda à monter sur le dos chaud du renne, avec les moufles.

s.t: "If you do not find your Kai, come back to me," she said.
s.fr: « Si tu ne trouves pas ton Kai, reviens vers moi, » dit-elle.

s.t: Gerda thanked the robber girl and the reindeer for her help, and her mittens.
s.fr: Gerda remercia la fille du brigand et le renne pour son aide, et ses moufles.

s.t: "Go and find your Kai," the robber girl said, and smiled.
s.fr: « Va et trouve ton Kai, » dit la fille du brigand, et elle sourit.

s.t: The reindeer ran out of the castle and into the forest, to the north.
s.fr: Le renne courut hors du château et dans la forêt, vers le nord.

paras.summary: She helps Gerda onto the reindeer's back, tells her to come back if she doesn't find Kai, and after Gerda thanks them both, sends her off with a smile as the reindeer runs out into the forest, north.

chapterList.title: Northward with the Reindeer
also: The Wise Woman of the North

s.t: The reindeer ran north through the cold night.
s.fr: Le renne courut vers le nord à travers la froide nuit.

s.t: Gerda put on the warm mittens from the robber girl, and was not afraid.
s.fr: Gerda mit les chaudes moufles de la fille du brigand, et n’eut pas peur.

s.t: Lights of many colors moved across the night sky.
s.fr: Des lumières de nombreuses couleurs traversèrent le ciel nocturne.

paras.summary: The reindeer runs north through the cold night as Gerda dons warm mittens, and colored lights move across the sky.

s.t: "The lights come from the cold north, from the Snow Queen," the reindeer said.
s.fr: « Les lumières viennent du froid nord, de la Reine des Neiges, » dit le renne.

s.t: "I saw her palace of ice," he said.
s.fr: « J’ai vu son palais de glace, » dit-il.

s.t: "It stood on ice, cold and white," said the reindeer.
s.fr: « Il se tenait sur la glace, froid et blanc, » dit le renne.

s.t: Gerda asked the reindeer if Kai was in the palace of ice.
s.fr: Gerda demanda au renne si Kai était dans le palais de glace.

s.t: The reindeer did not know.
s.fr: Le renne ne savait pas.

paras.summary: The reindeer says the lights come from the Snow Queen and describes her ice palace, cold and white, but cannot say if Kai is there when Gerda asks.

s.t: Gerda listened to the reindeer and grew a little afraid of the cold north.
s.fr: Gerda écouta le renne et devint un peu effrayée par le froid nord.

s.t: But she did not turn back.
s.fr: Mais elle ne fit pas demi-tour.

s.t: For many days and nights, the reindeer ran on.
s.fr: Pendant de nombreux jours et nuits, le renne continua sa course.

paras.summary: Gerda grows afraid but will not turn back, and the reindeer runs on for days.

s.t: At last, they came to a small house in the cold world.
s.fr: Enfin, ils arrivèrent à une petite maison dans le monde froid.

s.t: A wise woman lived there.
s.fr: Une femme sage vivait là.

s.t: The reindeer stopped at her house.
s.fr: Le renne s’arrêta à sa maison.

paras.summary: A small house appears at last, home to a wise woman; the reindeer stops.

s.t: The wise woman looked out at Gerda and the reindeer.
s.fr: La femme sage regarda Gerda et le renne par la fenêtre.

s.t: The house was small and warm, inside and out.
s.fr: La maison était petite et chaude, à l’intérieur comme à l’extérieur.

s.t: "Come inside, out of the cold," she said.
s.fr: « Entrez, venez vous mettre à l’abri du froid, » dit-elle.

s.t: Gerda told her the tale, from the mirror to the Snow Queen.
s.fr: Gerda lui raconta l’histoire, depuis le miroir jusqu’à la Reine des Neiges.

s.t: The wise woman listened to Gerda and said nothing.
s.fr: La femme sage écouta Gerda et ne dit rien.

paras.summary: The wise woman invites Gerda and the reindeer into her small, warm house, and after Gerda tells the whole tale from mirror to Snow Queen, the woman listens and says nothing.

s.t: "The Snow Queen's palace is many cold days north," she said.
s.fr: « Le palais de la Reine des Neiges est à plusieurs jours froids vers le nord, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Kai sits in that palace now, his heart cold from the splinter," she said.
s.fr: « Kai est assis dans ce palais maintenant, son cœur froid à cause de l’éclat, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Will you give Gerda magic to help her?" the reindeer asked.
s.fr: « Pouvez-vous donner à Gerda de la magie pour l’aider ? » demanda le renne.

s.t: "I have no more power to give her," the wise woman said.
s.fr: « Je n’ai plus le pouvoir de lui en donner, » dit la femme sage.

paras.summary: She says the palace lies many cold days north, where Kai sits with a cold heart, and when the reindeer asks for magic, she has none left to give.

s.t: "Her strength is her loving heart," said the wise woman.
s.fr: « Sa force est son cœur aimant, » dit la femme sage.

s.t: "That is more than any magic in the north," she said.
s.fr: « C’est plus que toute magie du nord, » dit-elle.

s.t: "Leave her before the palace," she told the reindeer.
s.fr: « Laisse-la devant le palais, » dit-elle au renne.

s.t: "From there, she will go on alone," the wise woman said.
s.fr: « De là, elle ira seule, » dit la femme sage.

s.t: The reindeer thanked her, and they went on into the cold.
s.fr: Le renne la remercia, et ils continuèrent dans le froid.

paras.summary: Since Gerda's strength is her loving heart, greater than any magic, the woman tells the reindeer to leave her before the palace to go on alone, and they go on.

s.t: The reindeer ran for two more days, and the cold grew worse and worse.
s.fr: Le renne courut pendant deux jours de plus, et le froid devint de plus en plus intense.

s.t: The reindeer came to the last of the cold world, and stopped.
s.fr: Le renne arriva au bout du monde froid, et s’arrêta.

s.t: "I will go no farther than this," the reindeer said.
s.fr: « Je n’irai pas plus loin que ceci, » dit le renne.

s.t: Gerda climbed down and thanked the reindeer, and he stopped there in the cold.
s.fr: Gerda descendit et remercia le renne, et il s’arrêta là dans le froid.

paras.summary: After two more days of worsening cold, the reindeer stops at the edge of the cold world, says he can go no farther, and Gerda climbs down to thank him.

s.t: She walked alone, through the wind and the snow.
s.fr: Elle marcha seule, à travers le vent et la neige.

s.t: The cold wind came at her from the north.
s.fr: Le vent froid venait vers elle du nord.

s.t: Her hands and feet grew cold in the wind, but she did not turn back.
s.fr: Ses mains et ses pieds devinrent froids dans le vent, mais elle ne se retourna pas.

s.t: At last, Gerda saw the walls of ice before her.
s.fr: Enfin, Gerda vit les murs de glace devant elle.

s.t: This was the Snow Queen's great palace of ice, cold and quiet.
s.fr: C’était le grand palais de glace de la Reine des Neiges, froid et silencieux.

paras.summary: Gerda walks on alone through wind and snow from the north, her hands and feet growing cold, until at last she sees the walls of the Snow Queen's great ice palace, cold and quiet.

s.t: Gerda walked through a door of ice and into the palace.
s.fr: Gerda passa par une porte de glace et entra dans le palais.

s.t: The floor was one great lake of frozen ice.
s.fr: Le sol était un grand lac de glace gelée.

s.t: Gerda called out for Kai, but no one called back.
s.fr: Gerda appela Kai, mais personne ne répondit.

s.t: She walked from room to room in the palace to look for Kai.
s.fr: Elle alla de pièce en pièce dans le palais pour chercher Kai.

s.t: She came at last to a great hall of ice.
s.fr: Elle arriva enfin dans une grande salle de glace.

paras.summary: She walks through a door of ice into the palace, its floor one great frozen lake, and calling for Kai with no answer, searches room to room to a great hall of ice.

s.t: Kai sat alone on the frozen lake.
s.fr: Kai était assis seul sur le lac gelé.

s.t: Kai was blue with cold, but he did not move.
s.fr: Kai était bleu de froid, mais il ne bougeait pas.

s.t: He did not feel the cold on his hands.
s.fr: Il ne sentait pas le froid sur ses mains.

s.t: Many pieces of ice lay by him, and Kai moved them, one by one.
s.fr: De nombreux morceaux de glace gisaient près de lui, et Kai déplaçait les morceaux un par un.

paras.summary: Kai sits alone on the frozen lake, blue with cold and unable to feel his hands, moving the many ice pieces by him one by one.

s.t: The Snow Queen had made Kai a promise.
s.fr: La Reine des Neiges avait fait à Kai une promesse.

s.t: Kai had to form one word to go free.
s.fr: Kai devait former un mot pour être libre.

s.t: The Snow Queen had promised him the world, and new skates.
s.fr: La Reine des Neiges lui avait promis le monde, et de nouveaux patins.

s.t: The word was "forever," but Kai did not form it.
s.fr: Le mot était « forever », mais Kai ne le forma pas.

s.t: He moved the pieces, and moved them back.
s.fr: Il déplaçait les morceaux, et les remettait en place.

paras.summary: The Snow Queen promised him the world and new skates if he could form one word, 'forever,' but he cannot, and only moves the pieces back and forth.

s.t: Kai's heart was cold, and he did not feel afraid.
s.fr: Le cœur de Kai était froid, et il ne ressentait pas de peur.

s.t: Gerda ran across the ice and called out to him.
s.fr: Gerda courut sur la glace et l’appela.

s.t: Kai looked up, but his face did not change.
s.fr: Kai leva les yeux, mais son visage ne changea pas.

s.t: He did not know her.
s.fr: Il ne la reconnut pas.

s.t: Gerda sat down by him and took his cold hands.
s.fr: Gerda s’assit près de lui et prit ses mains froides.

s.t: "Kai, it's me, Gerda," she said, but he only looked at his ice pieces.
s.fr: « Kai, c’est moi, Gerda », dit-elle, mais il ne regardait que ses morceaux de glace.

paras.summary: Kai's cold heart feels no fear; Gerda runs to him, takes his cold hands, and says her name, but his face does not change, for he no longer knows her, and he goes back to his pieces.

s.t: Gerda held Kai and cried, for his heart was cold.
s.fr: Gerda tint Kai et pleura, car son cœur était froid.

s.t: Her warm tears melted the splinter on his heart.
s.fr: Ses larmes chaudes fondirent l’éclat sur son cœur.

s.t: Kai's heart was warm again, and he looked at Gerda.
s.fr: Le cœur de Kai était de nouveau chaud, et il regarda Gerda.

s.t: His eyes had tears, and he cried.
s.fr: Ses yeux avaient des larmes, et il pleura.

paras.summary: Gerda holds Kai and cries, and her warm tears melt the splinter on his heart until it grows warm again.

s.t: His tears washed the splinter out of his eye.
s.fr: Ses larmes lavèrent l’éclat hors de son œil.

s.t: "Gerda!" Kai said, for he did not feel cold.
s.fr: « Gerda ! » dit Kai, car il ne sentait pas le froid.

s.t: Kai did not remember the Snow Queen, or the ice palace.
s.fr: Kai ne se rappelait plus la Reine des Neiges, ni le palais de glace.

paras.summary: His tears wash out the splinter; seeing Gerda, he feels no cold, and forgets the Snow Queen.

s.t: She held him again, and did not let go.
s.fr: Elle le tint de nouveau, et ne le lâcha pas.

s.t: The ice pieces moved by themselves.
s.fr: Les morceaux de glace bougèrent d’eux-mêmes.

s.t: One by one, the pieces went into the word.
s.fr: Une à une, les pièces entrèrent dans le mot.

paras.summary: She holds him tight, and the ice pieces move by themselves into the word.

s.t: The word was "forever."
s.fr: Le mot était « forever ».

s.t: "We must go before the Snow Queen comes back," Gerda said.
s.fr: « Nous devons partir avant que la Reine des Neiges revienne », dit Gerda.

s.t: Kai took Gerda's hand, and they ran out of the palace.
s.fr: Kai prit la main de Gerda, et ils coururent hors du palais.

paras.summary: The word is done; Gerda says they must go, and Kai takes her hand to run.

s.t: The reindeer stood in the snow before the palace.
s.fr: Le renne se tenait dans la neige devant le palais.

s.t: Kai and Gerda climbed onto his back, and he ran south.
s.fr: Kai et Gerda montèrent sur son dos, et il courut vers le sud.

s.t: Day by day, the snow grew thin.
s.fr: Jour après jour, la neige devint fine.

s.t: The snow was gone, and grass grew.
s.fr: La neige avait disparu, et l’herbe poussa.

s.t: At last, the reindeer took them to their town.
s.fr: Enfin, le renne les emmena dans leur ville.

paras.summary: The reindeer runs south with them on his back, the snow thinning until grass grows, and at last brings them to their town.

s.t: It was summer, and the sun was warm.
s.fr: C’était l’été, et le soleil était chaud.

s.t: Kai and Gerda thanked the reindeer.
s.fr: Kai et Gerda remercièrent le renne.

s.t: They walked to their house by the window.
s.fr: Ils marchèrent jusqu’à leur maison près de la fenêtre.

s.t: Grandmother sat in the sun, as before.
s.fr: Grand-mère s’assit au soleil, comme avant.

s.t: Their roses bloomed by the window, as they did each summer.
s.fr: Leurs roses fleurirent près de la fenêtre, comme chaque été.

paras.summary: It is summer; after thanking the reindeer, Kai and Gerda walk home, where grandmother sits in the sun as before and their roses bloom again.

s.t: Kai looked at Gerda and saw she had grown taller.
s.fr: Kai regarda Gerda et vit qu’elle avait grandi.

s.t: Gerda looked at Kai and saw he had grown taller.
s.fr: Gerda regarda Kai et vit qu’il avait grandi.

s.t: They had grown up, but in their hearts, they still felt like children.
s.fr: Ils avaient grandi, mais dans leurs cœurs, ils se sentaient encore comme des enfants.

s.t: Kai and Gerda sat by the roses again.
s.fr: Kai et Gerda s’assirent de nouveau près des roses.

paras.summary: Kai and Gerda see they have both grown taller, though in their hearts they still feel like children, and they sit by the roses again.
